_comment: THE PRE-LOOP OUTLET SWITCH MUST LEAVE A LOOP BEHIND -- MTG_COMBO_OFF_SWITCH_TRIAL.
Reconstructed from the user's own reference `claude_s2_gi1`, decision 14 (turn 4); it is the
COMBO OFF sweep's state R-b655effc8b, and before this fix it was the sweep's single worst
executor failure: a plan promising FIFTY blinks that ran ZERO.
Eldrazi Displacer is the outlet and Dimensional Infiltrator (a {1}{C} library-exile sink) is
already on the battlefield, so MTG_COMBO_OFF_OUTLET_SWITCH's two conditions hold -- the outlet
spends a {C} pip and a {C}-pip sink is live -- and Emiel the Blessed is sitting in hand. The
switch fired, paid Emiel's {2}{W}{W} out of the board, and left nothing:
[edf-loop] OUTLET SWITCH -> id=9 (pip-free, {C} sink live)
[edf-loop] k=0 enter  cost={3} float{} avail{}
[edf-loop] STOP at k=0: pay-failed
And the swap was not even needed: this loop's net_c is +1, so the Displacer was not starving on
colourless at all -- the switch was pure cost. The trigger is board INVENTORY (a pip outlet plus
a pip sink), which says nothing about whether the payment is affordable.
The switch now runs as a REAL TRIAL first, on a copy of the state and through the loop's own
payer: deploy the pip-free outlet, then require the NEW outlet's first activation to be payable.
Here it is not, the swap is declined, and the Displacer loop runs 49 of its 50 iterations and
decks the opponent.
A/B on this fixture (one binary):
default                          -> 49 blinks, COMBO OFF verified, opponent decked
MTG_COMBO_OFF_SWITCH_TRIAL=0     -> 0 blinks, offered but NOT verified, apply does not win
